title: Strong square-zero effectivity implies openness of versality
statement:
Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a category fibred in groupoids on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site]: equivalently, it assigns a groupoid $\mathcal F(T)$ to each scheme $T$, with pullback functors along scheme morphisms and coherent composition and identity isomorphisms. Assume the following four conditions. (1) For any scheme $T$ and $a,b\in\mathcal F(T)$, the presheaf $T'\mapsto\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal F(T')}(a|_{T'},b|_{T'})$ on $T$-schemes is represented by an algebraic space over $T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. (2) For all ring maps $A\to B\leftarrow B'$ with $B'\to B$ surjective and square-zero kernel, restriction induces an equivalence $\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}(A\times_B B'))\simeq\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A)\times_{\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}B)}\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}B')$. The groupoid on the right consists of two objects and a specified isomorphism of their restrictions, with pairs of arrows compatible with that isomorphism. (3) For every small directed inverse system of affine schemes $T_i$ with limit $T$, every object over $T$ descends to a stage, every isomorphism between stage objects descends to a sufficiently late common stage, and equality of stage isomorphisms over $T$ holds at a sufficiently late common stage. (4) For every inverse sequence of commutative rings $(R_n)_{n\geq1}$ whose maps $R_m\to R_n$ for $m\geq n$ are surjective with square-zero kernels, every compatible system $x_n\in\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}R_n)$ is effective: for $R=\varprojlim_n R_n$ there is an $x\in\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ with isomorphisms $x|_{\operatorname{Spec}R_n}\cong x_n$ compatible with all transition isomorphisms.

Then $\mathcal F$ satisfies openness of versality. Precisely, let $U$ be locally of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $x\in\mathcal F(U)$. A finite type point $u$ means that $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ is of finite type. Say that $x$ is versal at $u$ if for every surjection $A'\to A$ of Artinian local rings with residue field identified with $\kappa(u)$ and nilpotent kernel, every map $\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$ reducing to $u$, and every object $y'\in\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A')$ equipped with an isomorphism $y'|_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\cong x|_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$, there is a lift $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to U$ and an isomorphism $y'\cong x|_{\operatorname{Spec}A'}$ inducing the specified one. Here Artinian means that every descending chain of ideals stabilizes; all ring maps respect the indicated residue-field identifications. If $x$ is versal at a finite type point $u_0$, there is an open neighbourhood $U'$ of $u_0$ on which $x$ is versal at every finite type point.

source.place: Tag 0CXU (lemma-SGE-implies-openness-versality), specialized to Spec Z; remark-strong-effectiveness; definitions definition-RS-star, definition-limit-preserving, definition-versal and definition-openness-versality.

proof.text: Fix $U,x,u_0$ in the conclusion. Choose an affine neighbourhood of $u_0$ on which $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is of finite type, and replace $U$ and $x$ by their restrictions. Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$. This is permitted by the local finite type definition, and finding the required open inside this neighbourhood suffices for the original $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $U$ is Noetherian and $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian. Suppose for contradiction that no open neighbourhood of $u_0$ has the required versality. Let $E$ be the finite type points where $x$ is not versal. Every neighbourhood of $u_0$ meets $E$, hence $u_0\in\overline E$, whereas $u_0\notin E$.

source.place: Tag 0CXU (lemma-SGE-implies-openness-versality), first paragraph: affine restriction and the bad locus E.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-artin-versality-generalization] with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$. Its three assumptions are (1)--(3) of the item, and the Noetherian base is given in step 1. No $u\in E$ can specialize to $u_0$, since versality at $u_0$ would then imply versality at $u$. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-countable-antichain], choose an at most countable $D\subseteq E$ with $\overline D=\overline E$ and no specializations between distinct points. It is infinite: if $D$ were finite, $\overline D=\bigcup_{u\in D}\overline{\{u\}}$ would exclude $u_0$. Enumerate $D=\{u_1,u_2,\ldots\}$ without repetitions. Thus $u_0$ is in its closure and every term is a non-versal finite type point.

source.place: Tag 0CXU (lemma-SGE-implies-openness-versality), first paragraph: generalization, countable extraction and removal of specializations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-artin-nonversal-thickening-tower] to this sequence; condition (2) of the item is its square-zero gluing assumption. Obtain $U_n=\operatorname{Spec}R_n$ and $x_n$ with all transition isomorphisms and with the stated prohibition on local retractions at $u_n$. Put $R=\varprojlim_{n\geq0}R_n$. For $m\geq n$, an element of $\ker(R_m\to R_n)$ lies in $\ker(R_m\to R_0)$, whose square is zero; hence every transition kernel is square zero, including nonconsecutive ones. Restricting to indices $n\geq1$ does not change this limit: its $R_0$ coordinate is forced by its $R_1$ coordinate. Hypothesis (4) therefore supplies $\xi\in\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ with compatible identifications at all $n\geq0$, including $x_0=x$.

source.place: Tag 0CXU (lemma-SGE-implies-openness-versality), second paragraph: the tower and application of strong square-zero effectivity.

proof.text: The projection $R\to R_0$ is surjective: given an element of $R_0$, lift it recursively through each surjection $R_{n+1}\to R_n$. If $a,b$ lie in its kernel, their coordinates at $n$ lie in $\ker(R_n\to R_0)$, so every coordinate of $ab$ is zero. Thus $\ker(R\to R_0)^2=0$. The finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras of $R$, ordered by inclusion, are a small directed system and their union is $R$: any finite collection of elements belongs to the subalgebra it generates, and the sum and product operations agree there. Their inclusion cocone is colimiting by [lem-weil-pbc-directed-subalgebra-ring-colimit], since the union is all of $R$. The affine case of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] therefore identifies the scheme limit with $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Hypothesis (3) descends $\xi$ to some $x'\in\mathcal F(U')$ with $U'=\operatorname{Spec}R'$ for a finite type $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra $R'\subseteq R$.

source.place: Tag 0CXU (lemma-SGE-implies-openness-versality), second paragraph: the square-zero projection and finite type descent of xi.

proof.text: Choose finitely many $\mathbf Z$-algebra generators of $R_0$ and lifts in $R$. Adjoin these lifts to $R'$, pulling back $x'$ to the enlarged finite type subalgebra. Now $R'\to R_0$ is surjective and its kernel is square zero, being contained in $\ker(R\to R_0)$. Thus $j:U\hookrightarrow U'$ is a first order thickening. The projections $R\to R_n$ restrict to maps $R'\to R_n$ compatible with $R'\to R_0$; pulling back $x'$ along them yields the compatible isomorphisms $x_n\cong x'|_{U_n}$ already fixed through $\xi$. In particular fix the resulting $\theta:x\cong j^*x'$.

source.place: Tag 0CXU (lemma-SGE-implies-openness-versality), second paragraph: enlarge R prime and retain all compatibility isomorphisms.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-artin-versal-base-change-smooth] with the original $U,x$ and with $V=U',y=x'$. Conditions (1)--(3) are unchanged, both schemes are finite type over $\mathbf Z$, and $\theta$ gives its thickening-section case. Obtain the algebraic space $Z$ of triples $(a,b,\alpha:a^*x\cong b^*x')$, its projections $p:Z\to U$, $q:Z\to U'$, and $i:U\to Z$ with $pi=\operatorname{id}_U$, $qi=j$, and universal isomorphism restricting to $\theta$. The lemma states that $i(u_0)$ is a finite type point and provides an open $O\subseteq Z$ containing $i(u_0)$ on which $q$ is smooth. This invocation requires neither effectiveness for a completed Noetherian local ring nor an algebraic-stack assumption on $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Tag 0CXU (lemma-SGE-implies-openness-versality), paragraphs defining Z and z_0 and applying lemma-base-change-versal.

proof.text: Choose a principal open $V=D(f)\subseteq U$ containing $u_0$ and contained in $i^{-1}(O)$. Lift $f$ to $f'\in R'$ and put $V'=D(f')\subseteq U'$. The quotient $R'_{f'}\to (R_0)_f$ is surjective and square zero: a fraction in its kernel has numerator mapping to zero after multiplication by some power of $f$; multiply its numerator and denominator by that power to represent it by an element of the localized original kernel, whose square vanishes. Thus $V\hookrightarrow V'$ is a first order thickening of affine schemes. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-space-affine-infinitesimal-lift] to $q|_O:O\to U'$, $a_0=i|_V$ and the open inclusion $b:V'\to U'$. It gives $s:V'\to O$ with $qs=b$ and $s|_V=i|_V$.

source.place: Tag 0CXU (lemma-SGE-implies-openness-versality), shrinking paragraph and penultimate paragraph: explicit principal-open restriction and affine infinitesimal lifting.

proof.text: Put $r=ps:V'\to U$. The universal isomorphism at the triple $s$ gives $\beta:r^*x\cong x'|_{V'}$, whose restriction to $V$ is $\theta|_V$, and $r|_V$ is the open inclusion $V\to U$. Since $u_0\in\overline{\{u_n:n\geq1\}}$, choose $n$ with $u_n\in V$. Let $W$ be the inverse image of $V'$ in $U_n$ under its map to $U'$. It is an open neighbourhood of $u_n$ and $W\cap U=V$. Pull back $\beta^{-1}$ to $W$ and compose with $x_n|_W\cong x'|_W$. This gives an arrow $x_n|_W\to x$ over $W\to V'\xrightarrow r U$. On $V$, compatibility of the chosen reduction isomorphisms makes its composite with $x|_V\to x_n|_W$ the canonical restriction arrow $x|_V\to x$: the two factors are precisely $\theta$ and $\theta^{-1}$. This is forbidden at $u_n$ by [lem-sfb-artin-nonversal-thickening-tower]. The contradiction proves that an open neighbourhood with the required versality exists.

source.place: Tag 0CXU (lemma-SGE-implies-openness-versality), last paragraph: pull back the universal isomorphism, construct the forbidden local retraction and conclude.
